<thought>To identify the compound we need more structural clues. The 13C NMR shows 8 carbons (one duplicate), including a carbonyl (~167 ppm), two aromatic/sp² carbons (~144 and 130 ppm), a pair of equivalent aliphatic carbons (~34.5 ppm), and three distinct methyl‑type carbons (~22.8, 21.3, 19.2 ppm). The mass spectrum gives a protonated ion at m/z 141.115, corresponding to a neutral mass of ~140.107 Da. This suggests a formula near C₈H₁₂O₂ (140.084 Da) or a close isomer. The presence of a carbonyl and aromatic signals points to an aromatic ester or ketone with additional alkyl substituents. To narrow the possibilities, I will obtain the ¹H NMR spectrum, which will reveal the number and type of protons (aromatic vs aliphatic, multiplicities) and help confirm the substitution pattern.</thought>
